subproblems.title: A current vanishing on forms supported away from a compact set has compact support inside it
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, K ⊆ U compact, and F ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with F(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) whose topological support is disjoint from K. Then spt F ⊆ K and spt F is compact. Here spt F = U ∖ Z(F) (GeometricCurrentOn.support), Z(F) being the union of all open W with closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and F(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U K : Set (Euclid P)) (F : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) K → F ω = 0) → F.support ⊆ K ∧ IsCompact F.support

4. By dtc_blowUp_algebra (iv) (accepted: for λ > 0 and T ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U), ∂(blowUp T x λ) = blowUp (∂T) x λ) and ∂T = 0, we get ∂B_i = blowUp 0 x λ_i. (Equivalently, η_{x,λ_i#}0 evaluates the zero current on pulled-back forms.) Therefore currentEval(B_i, dω) = (blowUp 0 x λ_i)(ω_i) = 0 for all sufficiently large i.

subproblems.title: Mass of an integer multiplicity current equals its representing measure, and its support is the support of that measure
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P (= Euclid P) be open, let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation of T in U (an IMRep U n with R.Represents T, i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH^n(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), where H^n = μHE[n]). Write μ_R := R.measure = θ·H^n⌞M. Then: (a) M_W(T) = μ_R(W) for every open W ⊆ U, where M_W(T) = T.massOn W is the supremum (in [0, ∞]) of ofReal T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; (b) for every x ∈ U: x ∈ spt T if and only if μ_R(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0; (c) every other representation R' of T has the same measure: R'.measure = R.measure.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → T.massOn W = R.measure W) ∧ (∀ x ∈ U, (x ∈ T.support ↔ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → R.measure (ball x ε) ≠ 0)) ∧ ∀ R' : IMRep U n, R'.Represents T → R'.measure = R.measure
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note (context, not part of the numbered proof). This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dimred_im_mass_measure of DAG node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.im_mass_measure-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 01ae2c59e8d725f9f3839402fe6fe9bf93c32c3a). Its frozen type is byte-identical to the lean_statement above, so the controller links that node and creates no new one; registering it here overlays its accepted candidate history in this node's context (the proof base 00832a8f of the selected node contains only the frozen contract). Use in the selected node: step 5 (θ ≥ 1), which replaces the unregistered monotonicity (iv) by its own reviewed argument. With U := ℝ^P (open), T := C and an integer multiplicity representation R of C (first conjunct of IsMinimizingIn C univ), part (a) gives M_W(C) = R.measure(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P and part (b) gives R.measure(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for every x ∈ spt C and ε > 0. These are hypotheses (a) and (b) of the sibling support_density_lower_bound with μ := R.measure. The numbered proof below is that node's independently reviewed parent-supplied proof, reproduced unchanged; its 'parent' references are to that node's own parent.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.4–2.8 and Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 224–300 and 733–775), which state these facts as evident; this is the identity "μ_S = R.measure for every representation R, M_W(S) = μ_S(W), spt S = spt μ_S" used throughout the parent proof (its Notation paragraph). Notation: H^n := μHE[n]; for an n-covector α on ℝ^P, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})²)^{1/2}, the sum over strictly increasing multi-indices I = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n) (for n = 0, |α| = |α()|); dx^I is the dual basis covector.
1. (Pointwise duality.) Let τ_1, …, τ_n ∈ ℝ^P be orthonormal and let α be an n-covector. By multilinearity and alternation, α(τ_1, …, τ_n) = Σ_I α(e_I)·det(τ^I), where τ^I is the n × n matrix (⟨e_{i_a}, τ_b⟩)_{a,b}. By the Cauchy–Binet formula, Σ_I det(τ^I)² = det(τᵀτ) = det(I_n) = 1. Hence |α(τ_1, …, τ_n)| ≤ |α| by the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality, with equality for α_τ := Σ_I det(τ^I) dx^I, which satisfies |α_τ| = 1 and α_τ(τ_1, …, τ_n) = 1. (For n = 0 both sides equal |α()| and α_τ := 1.)
2. (Consequences for R.) By the field `orients` of IMRep, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M there are an orthonormal family τ(x) and a sign σ(x) ∈ {±1} with ξ(x)(α) = σ(x)·α(τ(x)) for every n-covector α (IsUnitOrientationOf). Hence, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all α. Moreover β(x) := Σ_I ξ(x)(dx^I)·dx^I equals σ(x)·α_{τ(x)} for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M, so |β(x)| = 1 and ξ(x)(β(x)) = 1 there. The coefficients ξ(·)(dx^I) of β are H^n⌞M-measurable because ξ is AEStronglyMeasurable for H^n⌞M (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient); as μ_R ≪ H^n⌞M, β is μ_R-measurable.
3. (Radon property.) μ_R is a Borel measure on ℝ^P with μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0 (M ⊆ U) and μ_R(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (field locallyIntegrable_mult). Since U is an open subset of ℝ^P, hence σ-compact, locally compact and second countable, the restriction of μ_R to U is a locally finite Borel measure on U and therefore outer regular by open sets and inner regular by compact sets on Borel subsets of U.
4. (Upper bound in (a).) Let W ⊆ U be open and let ω be admissible for M_W(T) (ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1 everywhere). By R.Represents T and step 2, T(ω) = ∫_M θ·ξ(ω) dH^n ≤ ∫_M θ·|ω| dH^n ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n = μ_R(W), because ω vanishes off W. Taking ofReal and the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W).
5. (Lower bound in (a).) Let W ⊆ U be open, K ⊆ W compact and ε > 0. By step 3 choose an open V with K ⊆ V, closure V compact and contained in W, and μ_R(V ∖ K) < ε. By Lusin's theorem (for the finite Radon measure μ_R⌞V and the μ_R-measurable map β of step 2, with values in the finite-dimensional space Λ^n of n-covectors) choose a compact K' ⊆ K with μ_R(K ∖ K') < ε and β|_{K'} continuous. Extend β|_{K'} to a continuous map ℝ^P → Λ^n (Tietze, coordinatewise) and compose with the retraction r(α) := α / max(1, |α|) (continuous, |r(α)| ≤ 1, r = id on the closed unit ball) to obtain a continuous β̃ with |β̃| ≤ 1 and β̃ = β on K'. Take χ ∈ C_c(V; [0, 1]) with χ = 1 on K, and put γ := χ·β̃ (continuous, |γ| ≤ 1, compact support in V). Let γ_j := γ * ϱ_{1/j} be the coordinatewise convolution with a standard mollifier. For all large j, γ_j is C^∞, tsupport γ_j is a compact subset of V ⊆ W ⊆ U, |γ_j| ≤ 1 everywhere (Jensen's inequality for the convex function |·|), and γ_j → γ uniformly. So γ_j is admissible for M_W(T) and M_W(T) ≥ ofReal T(γ_j). By dominated convergence (dominating function θ·1_{closure V}, integrable by step 3), T(γ_j) = ∫_M θ·ξ(γ_j) dH^n → ∫_M θ·ξ(γ) dH^n. On K', ξ(γ) = ξ(β) = 1 μ_R-a.e.; on V ∖ K', |ξ(γ)| ≤ 1; off V, γ = 0. Hence ∫_M θ·ξ(γ) dH^n ≥ μ_R(K') − μ_R(V ∖ K') ≥ (μ_R(K) − ε) − 2ε, since μ_R(V ∖ K') ≤ μ_R(V ∖ K) + μ_R(K ∖ K') < 2ε. Therefore M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(K) − 3ε for every compact K ⊆ W and every ε > 0, and inner regularity of μ_R on the open set W (step 3) gives M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(W) (also when μ_R(W) = ∞). Together with step 4, M_W(T) = μ_R(W).
6. ((b), "if".) Let x ∈ U with μ_R(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0, and suppose x ∉ spt T = U ∖ zeroRegion(T). Then x ∈ W for some open W with closure W compact and contained in U on which T vanishes, i.e. T(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W. Every admissible value in the definition of M_W(T) is ofReal 0 = 0 (and the zero form is admissible), so M_W(T) = 0, and by (a) μ_R(W) = 0. For ε > 0 so small that B_ε(x) ⊆ W we get μ_R(B_ε(x)) = 0, a contradiction. Hence x ∈ spt T.
7. ((b), "only if".) Let x ∈ spt T and suppose μ_R(B_ε(x)) = 0 for some ε > 0. Choose ε' ∈ (0, ε) with closedBall x ε' ⊆ U (U is open). W := B_{ε'}(x) is open, its closure closedBall x ε' is compact and contained in U, and for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W, step 2 gives |T(ω)| ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ·|ω| dH^n ≤ (sup_x |ω(x)|)·μ_R(W) = 0. So T vanishes on W, W belongs to the family defining zeroRegion(T), x ∈ zeroRegion(T), i.e. x ∉ spt T: a contradiction. Hence μ_R(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0.
8. ((c).) Let R' be another representation of T. By (a) applied to R and to R', R'.measure(W) = M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for every open W ⊆ U. Both measures vanish on ℝ^P ∖ U (both carriers lie in U) and are finite on every open W whose closure is a compact subset of U (step 3). The open subsets of U with compact closure in U form a π-system (closed under finite intersections) generating the Borel σ-algebra of U (every open subset of U is a countable union of them), and U is the union of an increasing sequence of them on which both measures are finite. By the uniqueness theorem for measures agreeing on such a generating π-system, R'.measure(A ∩ U) = R.measure(A ∩ U) for every Borel A, hence R'.measure = R.measure.
proof_key_steps: Cauchy–Binet duality: |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for the unit simple orientation ξ(x), with equality for the dual covector β(x).
Upper bound M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W) directly from the representation.
Lower bound by Lusin, Tietze extension, retraction to the unit ball, mollification and inner regularity of the Radon measure μ_R.
Support: T vanishes on W ⇔ M_W(T) = 0 ⇔ μ_R(W) = 0, giving spt T = spt μ_R inside U.
Representation independence: two representations agree on open subsets of U, hence (π-system uniqueness, σ-finiteness on U) everywhere.

subproblems.title: Lower bound 1 for every ball-density limit of an integer multiplicity weight at almost every point
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n) with weight μ := R.measure = θ·Hⁿ⌞M (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then the following holds for μ-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P. Whenever θ₀ ∈ ℝ and μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) → ofReal(θ₀) in [0, ∞] as ρ ↓ 0, θ₀ ≥ 1. Here ω_n = unitBallVolume n and B_ρ(x) = ball x ρ.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note (context, not part of the numbered proof). This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dimred_mono_ae_ball_density_ge_one of DAG node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.monotonicity-a1.ae_density_lower_bound-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit b59dbf93abbab37e4d13519ae2ffc6f0ad71f4c9). Its frozen type is byte-identical to the lean_statement above, so the controller links that node and creates no new one. Its two DAG prerequisites are comparator-accepted and are contained in that candidate history: Submission.rsd_tendsto_closedBall_density_of_approxTangent (node root.regular_set_dense-a1.density_eq_multiplicity-a1.unweighted_density_one-a1, candidate dbef2c15948a21d9574315bea458a9edb4f708e3) and Submission.rsd_tendsto_ball_density_of_closedBall (node root.regular_set_dense-a1.density_eq_multiplicity-a1.closed_to_open_ball_density-a1, candidate c3ca64f29e6259bb0947d084036f55b096f91e3f). In the numbered proof below, 'the sibling closed_ball_unit_density' is the first and 'the sibling open_ball_density' is the second (their keys in the split of root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.monotonicity-a1); their exact statements and reviewed proofs follow the main proof. Use in the selected node: step 5, with U := ℝ^P and an integer multiplicity representation R of C; its conclusion is hypothesis (c) of the sibling support_density_lower_bound with μ := R.measure. The numbered proof below is that node's independently reviewed parent-supplied proof, reproduced unchanged; its 'selected node' and 'sibling' references are to that node's own parent and siblings.

Source: the first half of step 7 of the selected node's supplied proof ("Θ ≥ 1 μ-a.e."), i.e. Simon Ch. 4, 3.13 and the sentence after it (chapter-04.txt lines 350–364), with Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(3) (chapter-03.txt lines 95–101). Only a lower bound is needed. So instead of Θⁿ(μ, x) = θ(x) (Ch. 3, Theorem 1.9 with Ch. 4, Remark 1.8(2)), we use θ ≥ 1 and the unit density of the unweighted measure Hⁿ⌞M, which is given by the siblings closed_ball_unit_density and open_ball_density.
Notation: M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ν := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M, μ := R.measure = ν.withDensity θ, ω_n := unitBallVolume n, B_t(z) := ball z t.
1. (Reduction to ν.) μ ≪ ν (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous). So every property that holds for ν-a.e. x holds for μ-a.e. x (AbsolutelyContinuous.ae_le). It suffices to prove the claim for ν-a.e. x.
2. (Good points.) M is Borel, so ν-a.e. x lies in M (ae_restrict_mem). By the field R.orients, for ν-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. Both properties hold simultaneously for ν-a.e. x.
3. (Weight versus area.) For every Borel A, ν(A) ≤ μ(A). Indeed μ(A) = ∫⁻_A θ dν (withDensity_apply). θ is ℕ-valued and positive on M (R.mult_pos), and ν-a.e. point lies in M, so θ ≥ 1 ν-a.e. Hence μ(A) ≥ ∫⁻_A 1 dν = ν(A).
4. (Local finiteness.) Fix x as in step 2, with x ∈ M and a subspace Q. Fix θ₀ ∈ ℝ with μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) → ofReal(θ₀) as ρ ↓ 0; we must show θ₀ ≥ 1. Since x ∈ M ⊆ U (R.carrier_subset) and U is open, there is s > 0 with closedBall x s ⊆ U. closedBall x s is compact, and θ ≥ 1 on M, so Hⁿ(M ∩ closedBall x s) = ∫⁻_{M ∩ closedBall x s} 1 dHⁿ ≤ ∫⁻_{M ∩ closedBall x s} θ dHⁿ < ∞. The last bound is the field R.locallyIntegrable_mult for K = closedBall x s.
5. (Unit density of ν.)
 - By the sibling closed_ball_unit_density, applied to M, x, Q and s (using step 4 and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q), Hⁿ(M ∩ closedBall x ρ)/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) → 1 as ρ ↓ 0.
 - Closed balls are Borel, so ν(closedBall x ρ) = Hⁿ(closedBall x ρ ∩ M) = Hⁿ(M ∩ closedBall x ρ) for every ρ (Measure.restrict_apply). Hence ν(closedBall x ρ)/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) → 1.
 - By the sibling open_ball_density, applied to ν, x and the limit 1, ν(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) → 1 as ρ ↓ 0.
6. (Comparison and conclusion.) By step 3 with A = B_ρ(x), ν(B_ρ(x)) ≤ μ(B_ρ(x)) for every ρ. Division by the same element of [0, ∞] is monotone (ENNReal.div_le_div_right), so ν(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) ≤ μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) for every ρ. The left side tends to 1 by step 5, and the right side tends to ofReal(θ₀) by assumption. The filter ρ ↓ 0 is nontrivial, so 1 ≤ ofReal(θ₀) (le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto'). Hence θ₀ ≥ 1 (ENNReal.one_le_ofReal). This holds for every such θ₀ and every x in the ν-full set of step 2, so by step 1 the claim holds for μ-a.e. x.

Cited accepted prerequisite 1 (Submission.rsd_tendsto_closedBall_density_of_approxTangent, used in step 5 above as 'the sibling closed_ball_unit_density'). Statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^P, x ∈ ℝ^P, Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P, and s > 0 with H^n(M ∩ B̄_s(x)) < ∞, where H^n = μHE[n]. Suppose Q is an approximate tangent space of M at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4, as formalized by HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q: dim Q = n, and for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as r ↓ 0. Here η_{x,r}(y) = r^{-1}(y − x) (blowUpMap), and the integrals are Bochner integrals for H^n restricted to the indicated sets. Then H^n(M ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) → 1 in [0, ∞] as ρ ↓ 0. Here B̄_ρ(x) is the closed ball, ω_n = unitBallVolume n is the Lebesgue measure of the unit ball of ℝ^n, and the quotient is taken in [0, ∞] with ρ^n entered via ENNReal.ofReal.
Its reviewed numbered proof, verbatim (the handoff's appended Lean realization is omitted):
Source: step 2 (Unweighted density) of the parent proof. This is Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(3) (chapter-03.txt lines 95-101), with Definition 1.4 at lines 77-84. In Definition 1.4 one chooses f with 0 ≤ f ≤ 1, f ≡ 1 on B_1(0) and f ≡ 0 off B_{1+ε}(0), and lets ε ↓ 0; this gives lim_{ρ↓0} (ω_nρ^n)^{-1} H^n(M ∩ B_ρ(x)) = 1. As in the parent proof, a second cut-off from inside gives the matching lower bound. Only closed balls are needed. The finiteness of H^n(M ∩ B̄_s(x)) is part of the standing hypothesis of Definition 1.4; it makes the Bochner integrals in the hypothesis genuine for small r. The proof covers n = 0 (ℝ^0 is a point and ω_0 = 1) without a separate case. If n > P, no subspace Q has dimension n, so the hypothesis cannot hold.

Notation: H^n = μHE[n] on ℝ^P; ω := unitBallVolume n, and w is ω as a real number. For r > 0, η_r := η_{x,r} = blowUpMap x r, ν_r := H^n⌞η_r(M), and μ_Q := H^n⌞Q. All balls are closed.

1. (ω_n.) ω = vol(B_1(0) ⊆ ℝ^n) is positive, being the measure of a nonempty open set (measure_ball_pos), and finite (measure_ball_lt_top). Hence w > 0 and ω = ofReal(w).

2. (Plane balls.) Since dim Q = n, reindexing an orthonormal basis of Q by Fin n gives a linear isometry ι : ℝ^n → ℝ^P with range Q. For t ≥ 0, ι(B̄_t(0)) = Q ∩ B̄_t(0), because |ι v| = |v| and ι maps onto Q. Three facts compute this measure:
- H^n is invariant under isometries (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image);
- H^n equals Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume);
- vol(B̄_t(0)) = t^n vol(B_1(0)) (Measure.addHaar_closedBall, with finrank ℝ^n = n).
Hence μ_Q(B̄_t(0)) = H^n(Q ∩ B̄_t(0)) = ω·t^n. This is finite, with real value w t^n.

3. (Scaling.) Let r > 0 and A ⊆ ℝ^P. Then η_r(A) = r^{-1}·(A − x). The translation y ↦ y − x is an isometry, and H^n(cS) = |c|^n H^n(S) (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀). So H^n(η_r(A)) = r^{-n} H^n(A). Moreover |η_r(z)| ≤ t ⟺ dist(z, x) ≤ tr, so η_r(M) ∩ B̄_t(0) = η_r(M ∩ B̄_{tr}(x)). Hence
 ν_r(B̄_t(0)) = H^n(η_r(M) ∩ B̄_t(0)) = r^{-n} H^n(M ∩ B̄_{tr}(x)).
In particular ν_r(B̄_t(0)) < ∞ whenever tr ≤ s, by monotonicity and the hypothesis H^n(M ∩ B̄_s(x)) < ∞.

4. (Cut-off functions.) For 0 < a < b let g_{a,b}(y) := max{0, min{1, (b − |y|)/(b − a)}}.
- g_{a,b} is continuous.
- It vanishes when |y| ≥ b, so its support lies in the compact ball B̄_b(0) and g_{a,b} ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ).
- 0 ≤ g_{a,b} ≤ 1, and g_{a,b} = 1 when |y| ≤ a.
Consequently 1_{B̄_a(0)} ≤ g_{a,b} ≤ 1_{B̄_b(0)} pointwise.

5. (Integrability.) Let ν' be a measure on ℝ^P with ν'(B̄_t(0)) < ∞. Then 1_{B̄_t(0)} is ν'-integrable, and by domination so is every continuous f with 0 ≤ f ≤ 1_{B̄_t(0)}. By steps 2-3 this applies to ν_r when tr ≤ s, to μ_Q for all t, and to the cut-offs of step 4. For such f, ∫ f dν' and ∫ 1_{B̄_t(0)} dν' = ν'(B̄_t(0)) (as a real number; integral_indicator_one) are genuine finite integrals, and integral_mono compares them.

6. (Normalised mass.) For r > 0 put a(r) := r^{-n}·H^n(M ∩ B̄_r(x)). This is a real number since H^n(M ∩ B̄_r(x)) < ∞ for r ≤ s. By step 3 with t = 1, the real value of ν_r(B̄_1(0)) is a(r).

7. (a(r) → w.) It suffices to show that, as r → 0 within (0, ∞), eventually c < a(r) for each c < w, and eventually a(r) < c for each c > w.
(i) Let c < w.
- The map ε ↦ w(1 − ε)^n is continuous with value w at 0. Pick ε ∈ (0, 1) with c < w(1 − ε)^n and let f₁ := g_{1−ε,1}.
- By steps 2, 4 and 5, ∫_Q f₁ dH^n ≥ ∫ 1_{B̄_{1−ε}(0)} dμ_Q = w(1 − ε)^n > c.
- By the hypothesis applied to f₁, ∫_{η_r(M)} f₁ dH^n → ∫_Q f₁ dH^n, so eventually ∫_{η_r(M)} f₁ dH^n > c.
- For 0 < r ≤ s/2 (so 1·r ≤ s), f₁ ≤ 1_{B̄_1(0)} gives ∫_{η_r(M)} f₁ dH^n ≤ ν_r(B̄_1(0)) = a(r) (steps 5 and 6).
Hence eventually a(r) > c.
(ii) Let c > w.
- Pick ε ∈ (0, 1) with w(1 + ε)^n < c and let f₂ := g_{1,1+ε}.
- ∫_Q f₂ dH^n ≤ ∫ 1_{B̄_{1+ε}(0)} dμ_Q = w(1 + ε)^n < c, so eventually ∫_{η_r(M)} f₂ dH^n < c.
- For 0 < r ≤ s/2 we have (1 + ε)r ≤ 2r ≤ s, so f₂ is ν_r-integrable (step 5).
- 1_{B̄_1(0)} ≤ f₂ gives a(r) = ν_r(B̄_1(0)) ≤ ∫_{η_r(M)} f₂ dH^n.
Hence eventually a(r) < c.
By the order-topology characterisation (tendsto_order), a(r) → w as r ↓ 0.

8. (Back to [0, ∞].) Let 0 < ρ ≤ s. Write H^n(M ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) = ofReal(m), where m is its (finite) real value; also ω = ofReal(w) and ω·ofReal(ρ^n) = ofReal(wρ^n) with wρ^n > 0. Then
 H^n(M ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/(ω·ofReal(ρ^n)) = ofReal(m/(wρ^n)) = ofReal(a(ρ)/w)
(ENNReal.ofReal_div_of_pos). Since a(ρ)/w → w/w = 1 and ofReal is continuous, ofReal(a(ρ)/w) → 1. The two functions agree on (0, s], a right-neighbourhood of 0, so the quotient tends to 1 as ρ ↓ 0. ∎

Cited accepted prerequisite 2 (Submission.rsd_tendsto_ball_density_of_closedBall, used in step 5 above as 'the sibling open_ball_density'). Statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let ν be any Borel measure on ℝ^P, x ∈ ℝ^P and θ ∈ [0, ∞]. Write ω_n = unitBallVolume n (the Lebesgue measure of the unit ball of ℝ^n) and, for ρ > 0, c(ρ) = ω_n·ρ^n ∈ [0, ∞], with ρ^n entered via ENNReal.ofReal. If ν(B̄_ρ(x))/c(ρ) → θ in [0, ∞] as ρ ↓ 0, then ν(B_ρ(x))/c(ρ) → θ as ρ ↓ 0. Here B̄_ρ(x) and B_ρ(x) are the closed and open balls, and quotients are taken in [0, ∞].
Its reviewed numbered proof, verbatim (the handoff's appended Lean realization is omitted):
Source: step 4 (Open balls) of the parent proof. Simon Ch. 1, 3.1-3.2 (chapter-01.txt lines 561-592) observes that the n-dimensional densities may be computed with closed balls B_ρ(x) or with open balls. The frozen contract's docstring for HasMassDensity says the same: open and closed balls give the same limit. The parent's argument is the sandwich B̄_{tρ}(x) ⊆ B_ρ(x) ⊆ B̄_ρ(x), followed by t ↑ 1. Here it is carried out in the order topology of [0, ∞], which also covers θ = ∞.

Notation: ω := unitBallVolume n and c(ρ) := ω·ofReal(ρ^n). Let g(ρ) := ν(B̄_ρ(x))/c(ρ) and h(ρ) := ν(B_ρ(x))/c(ρ), all in [0, ∞]. By hypothesis g(ρ) → θ as ρ → 0 within (0, ∞). Below, eventually always refers to ρ → 0 within (0, ∞). By the characterisation of convergence in the order topology of [0, ∞] (tendsto_order), it suffices to prove:
- (U) for every b > θ, eventually h(ρ) < b;
- (L) for every a < θ, eventually h(ρ) > a.

1. (Upper bound (U).) For every ρ, B_ρ(x) ⊆ B̄_ρ(x), so ν(B_ρ(x)) ≤ ν(B̄_ρ(x)). Dividing both by the same c(ρ) gives h(ρ) ≤ g(ρ). Given b > θ, eventually g(ρ) < b because g → θ. Hence eventually h(ρ) ≤ g(ρ) < b.

2. (Choice of a dilation factor.) Let a < θ.
- As t → 1 from below, ofReal(t^n) → ofReal(1) = 1, by continuity of t ↦ t^n and of ofReal.
- Hence ofReal(t^n)·θ → 1·θ = θ. Multiplication by the constant θ is continuous at the limit 1 because 1 ≠ 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.mul_const).
- Since a < θ, eventually (as t → 1⁻) a < ofReal(t^n)·θ; also eventually t ∈ (0, 1). Pick such a t.
Put τ := ofReal(t^n). Since 0 < t, τ ∈ (0, ∞), i.e. τ ≠ 0 and τ ≠ ∞. From a < τ·θ we get a/τ < θ (ENNReal.div_lt_iff).

3. (Rescaled ratio.) The map ρ ↦ tρ sends (0, ∞) into (0, ∞) and tends to 0 as ρ → 0, so it tends to 0 within (0, ∞). Composing with g → θ gives g(tρ) → θ as ρ → 0 within (0, ∞). Since a/τ < θ, eventually g(tρ) > a/τ.

4. (Scaling identity.) Let ρ > 0. Then (tρ)^n = t^n ρ^n with t^n ≥ 0, so ofReal((tρ)^n) = τ·ofReal(ρ^n) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul) and c(tρ) = ω·τ·ofReal(ρ^n). Two facts finish the computation:
- (ω·ofReal(ρ^n)·τ)^{-1} = (ω·ofReal(ρ^n))^{-1}·τ^{-1} (ENNReal.mul_inv, valid as τ ≠ 0, ∞);
- τ^{-1}·τ = 1 (ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel).
Together they give g(tρ)·τ = ν(B̄_{tρ}(x))/c(ρ).

5. (Lower bound (L).) Let ρ > 0 with g(tρ) > a/τ; this holds eventually by step 3. Since 0 < t < 1, tρ < ρ, so B̄_{tρ}(x) ⊆ B_ρ(x). Therefore
 a = (a/τ)·τ < g(tρ)·τ = ν(B̄_{tρ}(x))/c(ρ) ≤ ν(B_ρ(x))/c(ρ) = h(ρ).
The four relations use, in order:
- (a/τ)·τ = a (ENNReal.div_mul_cancel, τ ≠ 0, ∞);
- strict monotonicity of multiplication by τ ∈ (0, ∞) (ENNReal.mul_lt_mul_iff_left);
- step 4;
- monotonicity of ν.
Hence eventually h(ρ) > a.

6. Steps 1 and 5 give (U) and (L) for all b > θ and all a < θ. Hence h(ρ) → θ as ρ ↓ 0. ∎

1. Case n = 0. Let R represent T and suppose x₀ ∈ M (H^0 is counting measure, so the a.e. conditions on R hold at every point of M; M is locally finite since ∫_{M∩K}θ dH^0 < ∞). Testing T with a 0-form supported near x₀ shows x₀ ∈ spt T ⊆ N. Let S be represented by (M∖{x₀}, θ, ξ); S is integer multiplicity, SameBoundary holds trivially (n = 0), spt(S−T) = {x₀} ⊆ N ∩ U ∩ W for a small open ball W ⊂⊂ U, and M_W(S) = M_W(T) − θ(x₀) < M_W(T), contradicting minimality. So M = ∅, the first variation vanishes identically, and H := 0 works. Assume n ≥ 1 from now on.
2. Support facts. μ_T(U ∖ spt T) = 0, hence H^n(M ∖ N) = 0. Since N is a C¹ submanifold, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M the approximate tangent space T_xM exists, is the plane oriented by ξ(x) (definition of IMRep) and is contained in T_xN (approximate tangent spaces of subsets of a C¹ submanifold, Ch. 3 §1 and Ch. 2 §4); also div_M X(x) = trace(p_{T_xM}∘DX(x)) = tangentialDivergence (Ch. 4, 2.3).
3. Deformations (book: "φ = φ_t of 2.1 of Ch. 4 with U ∩ N in place of U"; Ch. 4, 2.5–2.6). Let X ∈ C¹_c(U; ℝ^{n+k}) be tangent to N on N ∩ U, K := spt X. X is globally Lipschitz, so it has a C¹ flow φ_t (t ∈ ℝ), each φ_t a C¹ diffeomorphism of U onto U with φ_t = id outside K. N ∩ U is relatively closed in U (because (N̄∖N) ∩ U = ∅) and X|_{N∩U} is a C¹ tangent field on the C² manifold N; integral curves of this tangent field are integral curves of X, so by uniqueness the orbit of a point of N ∩ U stays in N ∩ U (it cannot leave the relatively closed set N ∩ U while staying in K ∪ {x} ⊂ U). Hence φ_t(N ∩ U) ⊆ N ∩ U.
4. Competitors (book (2),(3)). Let S_t := φ_{t#}T, defined from the representation (Ch. 6, 2.24(2), 3.3–3.9): S_t = τ(φ_t(M), θ∘φ_t^{−1}, induced orientation), an integer multiplicity current in U. ∂S_t = 0: choose smooth diffeomorphisms φ^ε of U, equal to the identity outside a fixed compact set, with φ^ε → φ_t in C¹; then φ^ε_#T(dω) = T((φ^ε)^#dω) = T(d(φ^ε)^#ω) = 0 and φ^ε_#T(dω) → S_t(dω) by dominated convergence in the integral formula of 2.24(2). Since φ_t = id off K, spt T ⊆ N and φ_t(N ∩ U) ⊆ N ∩ U, spt(S_t − T) ⊆ K ∩ N is compact. For any open W with K ⊂ W ⊂⊂ U, minimality gives M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S_t) for all t.
5. First variation (book (1)). By the area formula (Ch. 6, 3.2(3), 3.3–3.5; Ch. 4, 1.7–1.8), M_W(S_t) = ∫_{M∩W} J^M φ_t θ dH^n. Since φ_t(x) = x + tX(x) + o(t) in C¹ uniformly on K, d/dt J^Mφ_t(x)|_{t=0} = div_M X(x) with uniform bounds on K, and θ is integrable on K; so t ↦ M_W(S_t) is differentiable at 0 with derivative ∫_M θ div_M X dH^n (Ch. 4, 2.2). The minimum at t = 0 forces this derivative to vanish: R.firstVariation X = 0. This is IsStationaryAlong N.
6. Mean curvature (Ch. 4, 2.7 and 3.14). Let X ∈ C¹_c(U; ℝ^{n+k}) be arbitrary. Choose an open V ⊂ U containing N ∩ spt X on which the nearest point projection π onto N is C¹ (N is C²), let P(z) be the orthogonal projection onto T_zN (C¹ in z ∈ N), χ ∈ C¹_c(V) with χ = 1 near N ∩ spt X, and X^T := χ·P(π(·))X. Then X^T ∈ C¹_c(U) is tangent to N on N ∩ U, so δV(X^T) = 0 by step 5. On N, X − X^T = X^⊥ is normal to N, and at H^n-a.e. x ∈ M (where T_xM ⊆ T_xN by step 2) div_M X^⊥ = −X·H_N(x), H_N(x) := Σ_{i=1}^n B_x(τ_i, τ_i) with τ_i an orthonormal basis of T_xM and B the second fundamental form of N (Ch. 2, 5.9; Ch. 4, 2.7). Hence δV(X) = −∫ X·H dμ_V with H := H_N on M ∩ N and 0 elsewhere (Borel). On a compact K ⊂ U, K ∩ N is compact (N ∩ U relatively closed), B is continuous, so |H| ≤ √n·sup_{K∩N}|B| μ_V-a.e. on K. This is HasLocallyBoundedMeanCurvature. (If ℓ = k, B = 0 and H = 0.)
